scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

problem_definition_history.requested_solution: SH-CS requested an AI agent that auto-answers dispute tickets and auto-fixes whatever is causing wrong bills.
symptoms: Monthly CRM dispute ticket volume rose from ~600 in Jun-Jul 2026 to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-03).
59% of disputed bills (1785/3025) are based on ACTUAL reads rather than ESTIMATED reads (E-04).
Field manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target across 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep (E-01).
problem_definition_history.root_problem: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled from ~600/month to 1180-1260/month in Aug-Sep 2026 (E-03), primarily because a billing-side defect — most plausibly a change to billing import validation rules — produces wrong bills even for the 59% of disputed accounts with accepted ACTUAL meter reads (E-04), while field route completion falling to 88% against a 95% target since August (E-01) adds a secondary stream of estimated-bill disputes. This is not a ticket-handling speed problem, since response times remain within SLA (E-02).

challenges.rationale: ER-1: premise E-04 revised by E-12: E-04 still shows the raw split of 3025 disputed bills: 1240 ESTIMATED and 1785 ACTUAL. It no longer supports that the ESTIMATED-read portion reflects field-manual-read/estimate-substitution failure (PR-CHAIN-3's secondary stream claim); E-12 shows that same 1240 is entirely AMI-channel and 95.5% billing-import-rejection driven, not field-route incompleteness, though the ACTUAL-read billing-side-defect premise (PR-ROOT) remains reinforced.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

F-01.statement: Field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 88% against a 95% target, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: Dispute response times across 2440 tickets: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-04.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1785 ACTUAL, 1240 ESTIMATED (3025 total).

F-05.statement: billing-db tariff_change_log returned zero records, indicating no tariff changes were logged during the review period.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 provides that the utility may request route priority changes, which are executed only after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log lagging_routes query returned 14 routes with individual completion values (sample: route R-00 at 0.70), giving route-level detail underlying the 88% aggregate completion rate.

F-08.statement: billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle returned 320 accounts across 40 distinct routes with fields account_id and route only.

F-09.statement: Of the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills, 1184 (AMI channel) had an AMI read received before cutoff but billing import rejected it as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, and 56 (AMI channel) had NO_READ_RECEIVED.

F-10.statement: billing-config validation_rule_changes log shows rule BV-17 (high-consumption check comparing raw register value with 12-month m3 history, unit_scaling=none) deployed 2026-08-01, coinciding with the dispute surge onset; rule BV-09 (label text) deployed 2026-03-02 is unrelated.

F-11.statement: mdms-export meter_firmware_units shows firmware v4.2 (rollout 2026-06) uses register_unit '0.1 m3' while firmware v3.x uses register_unit 'm3'.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-CS-AUTOFIX-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-response/throughput problem; deploying an AI agent to auto-answer tickets and auto-fix bills will resolve it.

H-RULE-CHANGE-BUG.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic bill errors (e.g., wrong read-type acceptance or estimate substitution logic), driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: A degradation in the vendor-run AMI/MDMS nightly export (H-MDMS-BILL) since August caused missing or invalid interval reads, forcing more bills onto estimate substitution and triggering disputes.

H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE.statement: Contracted field manual-read collection (H-FIELD-BILL) degraded or routes went incomplete since August, increasing estimate substitution and bill errors.

H-NONBILLING-TICKET-DRIVER.statement: Bill accuracy has not materially changed since August; the ticket volume increase stems from a non-billing factor (e.g., seasonal usage spikes, CRM/channel change, or SLA shift) rather than erroneous bills.

H-HIGHCONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE.statement: A billing import validation rule flags AMI reads as 'high consumption' and rejects them (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution even when a valid read was received, accounting for ~95% (1184/1240) of disputed estimated bills (E-12).

H-BV17-UNITSCALE.statement: BV-17's high-consumption check compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13), which could falsely flag normal consumption as 'high' for meters whose raw register units differ from m3, explaining the 1184 REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION cases (E-12).

H-BV17-ACTUALBILL-OVERCALC.statement: The same v4.2 firmware register-unit mismatch (0.1 m3 vs m3, E-14) that triggers REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION for estimate-substitution cases may also cause BV-17 to miscompute (overstate ~10x) consumption for ACCEPTED ACTUAL reads from v4.2 meters, producing wrong ACTUAL-read bills (U-ACTUALDEFECT).

interpretation_history.interpretation: Field manual-read route completion for Aug-Sep 2026 was 88%, below the 95% target, across 9200 manual-read accounts, indicating a real shortfall in field read collection during the dispute-surge window.

E-01 still shows field manual-read route completion was 88% against a 95% target across 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026 — that measured shortfall stands as a fact. It no longer supports that this shortfall is the mechanism generating the disputed-estimated-bill stream in PD-1's root_problem (PR-CHAIN-3), since E-12 shows the 1240 disputed estimated bills are AMI-channel and billing-import-rejection driven, not attributable to field-manual-read incompleteness.
Across 2440 dispute tickets, median response was 1.6 days and p90 was 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA — ticket handling speed is not currently breaching its target.

Monthly dispute volume rose from ~600/month in June-July 2026 to 1180 in August and 1260 in September 2026, confirming the roughly-doubling surge and its August onset referenced in the initial request, as an authoritative, complete CRM measurement rather than a stakeholder claim.

Of 3025 disputed bills, 1785 (59%) were based on ACTUAL reads and 1240 (41%) on ESTIMATED reads, so most disputed bills did NOT result from estimate substitution. This weakens the estimate-substitution causal chain (AMI delivery failure, field-read failure) as the primary surge driver and points toward a billing-side defect affecting accepted actual reads as well.

E-04 still shows the raw split of 3025 disputed bills: 1240 ESTIMATED and 1785 ACTUAL. It no longer supports that the ESTIMATED-read portion reflects field-manual-read/estimate-substitution failure (PR-CHAIN-3's secondary stream claim); E-12 shows that same 1240 is entirely AMI-channel and 95.5% billing-import-rejection driven, not field-route incompleteness, though the ACTUAL-read billing-side-defect premise (PR-ROOT) remains reinforced.

The billing-db tariff_change_log query returned zero records for the review period, indicating no tariff changes were made, which rules out a tariff change as a contributing cause of the billing dispute surge; it does not speak to any currently listed hypothesis.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL's statement that no tariff change occurred this year corroborates the already-recorded authoritative finding E-05 (billing-db tariff_change_log, zero records), but as a non-authoritative stakeholder claim it adds no new evidentiary weight and does not speak to any currently listed hypothesis.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims field reading has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated (rather than actual) bills for the affected customers. This is an unverified stakeholder claim offering a specific mechanism for route incompleteness, from a source whose incentive is a contract headcount increase.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract (E-08) confirms the utility can request field route priority changes but they are only executed after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, matching the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint on push_route_update rather than revealing anything new about the dispute-surge root cause.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log's lagging_routes query authoritatively identifies 14 distinct routes each with a measured completion value (sample R-00 at 0.70), giving granular route-level detail behind the aggregate 88% completion shortfall already in evidence (E-01); this is useful for scoping which routes a push_route_update would target, but does not itself speak to why routes are lagging or to the billing-side defect.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle query, run as the designated AMI/MDMS proxy check, returned only account_id and route fields (320 accounts across 40 distinct routes) with no read-type or import-status data, so it cannot actually distinguish an AMI delivery cause from a field-read cause. It does show that estimated-last-cycle accounts span 40 routes, substantially more than the 14 routes already identified as lagging (E-09), indicating estimate substitution is broader than just the known field-lagging routes.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI (non-authoritative stakeholder message) claims vendor ticket TX-4471 has provisioned MDMS export access for Lakeside as of today. This is an unverified claim about tool access state, not new evidence about AMI read delivery itself; it does not change why E-04/E-10 show the dispute surge is primarily billing-side, but it suggests the previously ACCESS_PENDING mdms-export query may now be runnable to directly test U-MDMSACCESS.

E-12 (mdms-export, AMI read events for the 1240 disputed ESTIMATED bills from E-04) shows the counts sum exactly to 1240 and both records are read_channel=AMI: 1184 (95.5%) had a valid AMI read received before cutoff but billing import rejected it with status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, still exporting an estimated bill; 56 (4.5%) genuinely had NO_READ_RECEIVED. This means the disputed-estimated population is entirely AMI-metered, not field-manual-read, and is dominated by a billing-import validation rejection rather than true read-delivery failure.

E-13.content: billing-config.validation_rule_changes → 2 record(s): {"change": "high-consumption check compares raw register value with 12-month m3 history", "deployed": "2026-08-01", "rule": "BV-17", "unit_scaling": "none"}; {"change": "label text", "deployed": "2026-03-02", "rule": "BV-09"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: E-13 (AUTHORITATIVE, COMPLETE billing-config log) shows validation rule BV-17 — the high-consumption check comparing raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling "none" — was deployed 2026-08-01, exactly coinciding with the dispute surge onset and matching the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION mechanism already seen in E-12. The other logged change (BV-09, label text) is dated 2026-03-02 and is unrelated to the surge.

mdms-export's meter_firmware_units record shows v4.2 meters (rolled out 2026-06) report raw register values in units of "0.1 m3", while legacy v3.x meters report in "m3". Since BV-17 (E-13) compares raw register values directly against m3-based 12-month history with unit_scaling "none", this unit mismatch is a concrete mechanism by which v4.2 reads would appear ~10x their actual consumption, matching the REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION outcomes in E-12.

Field manual-read route completion is 88% against a 95% target (E-01), but the disputed-estimated-bill population is entirely AMI-channel, not field-manual-read (E-12), so this shortfall is an unrelated field-ops issue, not part of this problem's mechanism.
problem_definition.root_problem: Monthly CRM dispute ticket volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-03), substantially because billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3-based consumption history with no unit scaling; since v4.2 meter firmware (rollout 2026-06) reports register values in 0.1 m3 while legacy firmware reports in m3 (E-14), this mismatch causes valid AMI reads to be misclassified as high consumption and rejected (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution despite a valid read existing. This mechanism accounts for 1184 of 1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED-read bills (E-12), coinciding with the August surge onset (E-13). The cause of the remaining dispute volume tied to ACTUAL-read bills (1785/3025, E-04) is not yet established and is not asserted here.

proposal.root_problem: Monthly CRM dispute ticket volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul 2026) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep 2026) (E-03), substantially because billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), compares raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3-based consumption history with no unit scaling; since v4.2 meter firmware (rollout 2026-06) reports register values in 0.1 m3 while legacy firmware reports in m3 (E-14), this mismatch causes valid AMI reads to be misclassified as high consumption and rejected (REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION), forcing estimate substitution despite a valid read existing. causal_chain: Billing import validation rule BV-17 is deployed 2026-08-01, comparing raw AMI register values directly against 12-month m3-based consumption history with no unit scaling (E-13).
v4.2 meter firmware (rollout 2026-06) reports register values in units of 0.1 m3 while legacy v3.x firmware reports in m3 (E-14), creating a ~10x mismatch for v4.2 meters under BV-17's comparison.

This mismatch causes valid AMI reads from v4.2 meters to be misclassified as abnormally high consumption and rejected during billing import as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, even though 1184/1240 (95.5%) had a valid read received before cutoff (E-12).
Rejected reads force estimate substitution instead of using the legitimate AMI read, producing an estimated bill for an account that actually had a valid read.

The resulting estimated bills (plus the smaller 56/1240 genuine NO_READ_RECEIVED cases) drive dispute tickets, inflating monthly CRM dispute volume from the ~600/month baseline to 1180-1260/month beginning in August, coincident with BV-17's deployment date (E-03, E-13).

key_points: Problem as currently defined (PD-1@v2, superseding invalidated PD-1@v1): monthly CRM dispute volume rose from ~600/month (Jun-Jul) to 1180-1260/month (Aug-Sep) (E-03), substantially because billing rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01 (E-13), compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 history with no unit scaling; v4.2 meter firmware reports in 0.1 m3 while legacy reports in m3 (E-14), so valid reads get misclassified REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION, accounting for 1184/1240 (95.5%) disputed ESTIMATED bills (E-12).

This replaced the original requester framing (SH-CS's claim CL-01 that an AI auto-fix agent would solve a ticket-response problem): response times are within SLA (E-02), so that hypothesis (H-CS-AUTOFIX-FRAMING) was REJECTED.

The problem was established by testing competing hypotheses: field-staffing (H-FIELD-READ-FAILURE, resting partly on SH-FIELD's self-interested claim E-07) was REJECTED once E-12 showed the disputed-estimated population is entirely AMI-channel, not field-manual-read; AMI-delivery failure (H-AMI-DELIVERY-FAILURE) was also REJECTED. This triggered dependency review DR-1 and invalidated earlier assumptions A-RULECHANGE and A-FIELDSTAFF.

The confirmed mechanism is H-HIGHCONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE (CONFIRMED) and H-BV17-UNITSCALE (SUPPORTED), resting on E-12, E-13, E-14; the cause of the remaining disputed ACTUAL-read bills (1785 of 3025 total, E-04) is explicitly not yet established.
Release decision: HOLD. Nothing was released this cycle.

Reason for HOLD: a critical, OPEN verification obligation (VOB-R-6, blocking scope ENTIRE_SOLUTION, required before release) intersects the solution's sole release-scope item (identify_billing_rule_authority:SH-BILL). VOB-R-6 asks whether scope should be expanded to include an interim manual bill-credit fix (SR-INTERIM-MANUAL-BILLWRITE-REL) for the known affected accounts, and that question is unresolved.

The DEFINE Gate for PD-1@v2 ended CONDITIONAL_PASS, with several verification obligations OPEN outside the release scope: VOB-U-ACTUALDEFECT (cause of wrong ACTUAL-read bills), and VOB-R-3/VOB-U-RULEAUTHORITY (who holds write authority over billing-config to patch rule BV-17).

A structural fix exists but was not released: patching rule BV-17 (SR-PATCH-BV17-UNITSCALE) and asking vendor Telemetrix to standardize firmware units (SR-VENDOR-FIRMWARE-UNIT-STANDAR) are both marked not feasible within contest time; even identifying rule-change authority would not allow deployment, since billing-config is a read-only tool surface in this harness.

proposal.summary: The problem was redefined (PD-1@v2) as monthly dispute tickets roughly doubling since August (E-03) because billing validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-13) compares raw AMI register values to m3 history without unit conversion, misclassifying valid reads from newer v4.2 meters (which report in 0.1 m3, E-14) as high consumption and rejecting them — explaining 95.5% of disputed estimated bills (E-12). This superseded an earlier theory blaming field-staffing/route completion, invalidated once E-12 showed the affected accounts were entirely AMI-metered, and it rejected the original requester's (SH-CS) framing that an auto-answering AI agent would fix a response-speed problem, since response times are within SLA (E-02). The release decision is HOLD: nothing was released. This is because a critical, open verification obligation (VOB-R-6) about whether to add an interim manual bill-credit fix for the known affected accounts intersects the only scope item ready for release (identifying who holds billing-rule-change authority), and other open verification questions (who can patch BV-17, what causes wrong ACTUAL-read bills) remain unresolved and are tracked for a future cycle.
